LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.1: Length
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Length, part of Measurement in Grade 5 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you measure distance? 2. 2. Why should you measure distance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the kilometre as a unit of measuring length real life,

2. team up with peers to estimate distance in kilometres,

3. work with peers to establish the relationship between the kilometre and metre,

4. express the distance from kilometres to metres and metres to kilometres,

5. carry out addition involving distance in kilometres and metres,

6. carry out subtraction involving distance in kilometres and metres, 1. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the kilometre as a unit of measuring length real life,
2. team up with peers to estimate distance in kilometres,
3. work with peers to establish the relationship between the kilometre and metre,
4. express the distance from kilometres to metres and metres to kilometres,
5. carry out addition involving distance in kilometres and metres,
6. carry out subtraction involving distance in kilometres and metres, 1. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Length together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Integrity: learner measures and honestly records estimated distances practically using ropes and other learning materials.

● Respect: learner takes turn in measuring distance in kilometres practically using ropes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learner observes safety precautions while handling measuring instruments.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate measurement of length to construction a food preservation equipment in Agriculture.
